note: "They will perish, but You remain; they will all wear out like a garment" (Ps 102:26), quoted in Hebrews 1:11-12: "like a garment they will be changed". The psalmist speaks to God; the heavens are named in 102:25.
"they will all wear out like a garment"; the earth's foundations are named in 102:25.
"the earth will wear out like a garment" (the heavens, in the same verse, are likened to smoke).
"He wraps Himself in light as with a garment"; the ground is light worn like clothing.
"he will wrap himself with the land of Egypt as a shepherd wraps himself in his garment, and he will depart from there unscathed"; the ground is how easily he takes the land.

"May it be like a robe wrapped about him, like a belt tied forever around him." The "it" is the curse of the preceding verses; the card does not carry Ps 109:18, where he "clothed himself with cursing".
"all our righteous acts are like filthy rags"; the nearest record is righteousness, the verse says righteous acts.
